title: q-Analog Binomial Coefficients in Quantum Groups

problemStatement.formal: Define q-numbers [n]_q, q-factorials [n]_q!, and q-binomial coefficients [n choose k]_q over a commutative ring R, and prove [n,k]_1 = C(n,k).
problemStatement.plain: Formalize the q-analog (Gaussian) binomial coefficients, which generalize ordinary binomial coefficients by introducing a parameter q. When q=1, they recover the classical coefficients. When q is a prime power, they count subspaces of vector spaces over finite fields.
whyMatters: q-binomial coefficients are fundamental in combinatorics, quantum groups, and representation theory
They count k-dimensional subspaces of F_q^n, connecting algebra to finite geometry
The specialization theorem validates the generalization

knowledge.progressSummary: COMPLETED+EXTENDED: Full formalization of q-analog binomial coefficients with symmetry. Original formalization (q-numbers, q-factorials, q-binomials, specialization at q=1, product formula, absorption identity) extended with: (1) penultimate entry identity, (2) row absorption identity, (3) SYMMETRY of q-binomial coefficients over arbitrary CommRing. Also fixed bug in absorption proof.

insights: Recursive q-Pascal definition avoids division, works over any CommRing
Product formula proof requires q-number splitting lemma and case split on k=n vs k<n
q-binomial coefficients are polynomials in q with non-negative integer coefficients
No existing q-analog infrastructure in Mathlib v4.26.0 - built from scratch
Row absorption identity relates adjacent entries: [n,k]·[n-k] = [n,k+1]·[k+1], provable by induction + q-number splitting
Symmetry over arbitrary CommRing requires row absorption + geometric identity (cannot cancel q-factorials due to zero divisors)
Penultimate entry [n+1,n] = [n+1] proved via geometric sum identity: qNumber n + q^n = qNumber (n+1)
Fixed pre-existing bug in qBinom_absorption: case split needed for k=n boundary (IH requires k+1 ≤ n, not k+1 ≤ n+1)
